prompt: A fixed-frame, loss-free sliding-window sender just keeps its link busy. The link rate doubles while frame size and propagation RTT stay fixed. What adjustment may be needed?

options.text: A smaller window, because fewer frames fit into the feedback interval
options.explanation: At a higher rate, more frames can be transmitted before feedback returns.

options.text: No adjustment is ever needed because the route is unchanged
options.explanation: The route is unchanged, but each frame takes less time to transmit.

options.text: A larger frame window so the sender does not exhaust its allowance before ACKs return
options.explanation: Correct. Higher rate increases how many frame transmissions fit into the feedback cycle.

options.text: Sequence numbers can be reused immediately because the physical rate is higher
options.explanation: Faster sending does not remove ambiguity from old duplicates; safe reuse has its own constraints.

workedExample: Keep the feedback delay fixed and shorten each frame's transmission time. The sender can now finish its allowed frames sooner, potentially becoming idle before the first ACK returns. A larger allowance can cover that gap in the stated loss-free model. Queueing, ACK transmission and real recovery behaviour can change the required size.
